questions.question: In which state was the Rajkot English School located where Gandhi received his early education?
questions.explanation: Gandhi received his early education at Rajkot English School in the state of Gujarat.

questions.question: What was Rajkot English School renamed after independence in 1947?

options.A: Father of the Nation High School

questions.explanation: After independence in 1947, the school was renamed the 'Mohandas Gandhi High School'.

questions.question: According to the lead-in, in which subject was Gandhi noted to be weak?
questions.explanation: Gandhi was noted to be good at English, fair in Arithmetic, and weak in Geography.

questions.question: What was Gandhi's reaction whenever he won prizes and scholarships?
questions.explanation: He was astonished whenever he won prizes and scholarships.

questions.question: From which chapter of Gandhi's autobiography is this text an extract?
questions.explanation: The text describes Gandhi's high school days as described in Chapter 5 of his autobiography.

questions.question: To whom were the certificates of progress and character sent every year?
questions.explanation: Certificates of progress and character used to be sent to the parents every year.

questions.question: In which standards did Gandhi obtain scholarships of rupees four and ten respectively?
questions.explanation: In the fifth and sixth standards, he obtained scholarships of rupees four and ten respectively.

questions.question: What did Gandhi thank more than his merit for his achievement in winning scholarships?
questions.explanation: He stated it was an achievement for which he had to thank good luck more than his merit.

questions.question: What did Gandhi 'jealously guard' during his school days?
questions.explanation: Gandhi wrote, 'But I very jealously guarded my character'.

questions.question: What would draw tears from Gandhi's eyes?

options.C: The least little blemish on his character

questions.explanation: The text states, 'The least little blemish drew tears from my eyes'.

questions.question: How did Gandhi feel when he merited or seemed to merit a rebuke from his teacher?
questions.explanation: When he merited a rebuke, it was 'unbearable' for him.

questions.question: In which standard did Gandhi remember receiving corporal punishment for the first time?
questions.explanation: He remembers receiving corporal punishment when he was in the first or second standard.

questions.question: Who was the headmaster when Gandhi was in the seventh standard?
questions.explanation: Dorabji Edulji Gimi was the headmaster then.

questions.question: Which activities were made compulsory for the boys of the upper standards by the headmaster?
questions.explanation: The headmaster made gymnastics and cricket compulsory for the boys of upper standard.

questions.question: What was one of the reasons for Gandhi's 'aloofness' from compulsory physical exercises?
questions.explanation: Gandhi mentions, 'My shyness was one of the reasons for this aloofness'.

questions.question: What false notion did Gandhi have about gymnastics in school?

options.B: It had nothing to do with education.
options.D: It was a waste of money.

questions.explanation: He had the false notion that gymnastics had nothing to do with education.

questions.question: In his later years, Gandhi realized that physical training should have as much place in the curriculum as ______.
questions.explanation: He later knew that physical training should have much place in the curriculum as mental training.

questions.question: What was Gandhi's keen desire that made him dislike compulsory exercise?

options.B: To serve as nurse to his father

questions.explanation: The reason for his dislike was his 'keen desire to serve as nurse to my father'.

questions.question: What did Gandhi do as soon as the school closed?

options.B: He would hurry home and begin serving his father.

questions.explanation: As soon as school closed, he would hurry home to serve his father.

questions.question: Why did Gandhi reach school late for gymnastics one Saturday afternoon?

options.B: He had no watch and the clouds deceived him.
options.C: He was stopped by his father.

questions.explanation: He had no watch, and the clouds deceived him, leading him to reach school after the boys had left.

questions.question: What time was the gymnastics class scheduled for on that particular Saturday?
questions.explanation: He had to come from home to school for gymnastics at four o'clock in the afternoon.

questions.question: What was the fine ordered by Mr. Gimi for Gandhi's absence?
questions.explanation: Mr. Gimi refused to believe him and ordered him to pay a fine of one or two annas.

questions.question: What was Gandhi 'convicted' of, which deeply pained him?
questions.explanation: He was convicted of lying, which deeply pained him.

questions.question: What lesson did Gandhi learn from the incident where he was accused of lying?

options.A: A man of truth must also be a man of care.
options.B: A man should always carry a watch.
options.C: He should never trust a headmaster.

questions.explanation: Gandhi realized that 'a man of truth must also be a man of care'.

questions.question: How did Gandhi eventually obtain exemption from physical exercise?

options.B: His father wrote to the headmaster.

questions.explanation: The exemption was obtained as his father wrote himself to the headmaster saying he wanted Gandhi at home after school.

questions.question: Where was Gandhi when he realized that good handwriting is a necessary part of education?
questions.explanation: When he was in South Africa, he saw the beautiful handwriting of others and felt ashamed of his own.

questions.question: According to Gandhi, bad handwriting should be regarded as a sign of ______.
questions.explanation: He saw that 'bad handwriting should be regarded as a sign of an imperfect education'.

questions.question: What art does Gandhi believe children should be taught before learning to write?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's opinion was that 'children should first be taught the art of drawing before learning to write'.

questions.question: Why did Gandhi consider Sanskrit harder than geometry?

options.B: Sanskrit required everything to be learnt by heart.

questions.explanation: He thought in geometry there was nothing to memorise, whereas in Sanskrit 'everything had to be learnt by heart'.

questions.question: In which standard was the subject of Sanskrit commenced?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'This subject was also commenced from the fourth standard'.

questions.question: How did Gandhi describe the Sanskrit teacher in the text?
questions.explanation: The teacher was a 'hard taskmaster', as Gandhi thought.

questions.question: Why was Gandhi tempted to sit in the Persian class?

options.C: Boys said Persian was very easy.
options.D: He wanted to learn a new script.

questions.explanation: The 'easiness' of Persian as discussed by other boys tempted him.

questions.question: What did the Sanskrit teacher remind Gandhi regarding his religious background?

options.B: He was the son of a Vaishnava father.
options.C: He was a leader of the nation.
options.D: He was a student of truth.

questions.explanation: The teacher asked, 'How can you forget that you are the son of a Vaishnava father?'.

questions.question: Who was the Sanskrit teacher that Gandhi thanked with gratitude in his later life?
questions.explanation: Gandhi writes, 'Today I cannot but thank with gratitude of Krishnashankar Pandya'.

questions.question: Why was the study of Sanskrit important for Gandhi in his later life?

options.B: To take interest in sacred books

questions.explanation: Without that little Sanskrit, he would have 'found it difficult to take any interest in our sacred books'.

questions.question: What does the word 'rebuke' mean in the context of paragraph 2?

options.C: An expression of sharp disapproval or criticism

questions.explanation: In context, a rebuke is criticism from a teacher that Gandhi found unbearable.

questions.question: The word 'blemish' in the text refers to a ______.
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'blemish' as a moral defect.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'be none the worse' used in paragraph 5?

options.B: To be not harmed or affected by something

questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'be none the worse' as to not be harmed/affected by something.

questions.question: What does the term 'notion' mean as used in paragraph 5?
questions.explanation: Glossary: notion - an impression, an idea.

questions.question: According to the vocabulary section, 'unbearable' is formed by adding which negative prefix to 'bearable'?
questions.explanation: The prefix 'un' is added to the beginning of 'bearable' to make it 'unbearable'.

questions.question: Which of these words uses the prefix 'dis' to form its opposite, as shown in the exercises?
questions.explanation: The text gives the example: disobedient = dis + obedient.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Before I reached the school, the boys had all left', which event took place first?
questions.explanation: The Past Perfect 'had all left' indicates the event that took place earlier than the Simple Past 'reached'.

questions.question: According to the grammar section on conditional clauses, which structure talks about 'impossible, unreal or imaginary events in the past'?

options.B: If + had + V-en, would + have + V-en

questions.explanation: The structure If + S + had not + V-en, S + should/would + have + V-en is used for unreal conditions in the past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'She was deeply ashamed ______ her behavior at the party.'
questions.explanation: The exercise uses the preposition 'of' with ashamed.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Charities are exempted ______ paying tax.'
questions.explanation: The glossary and exercises use 'exempt from'.

questions.question: What does the word 'commence' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: commence - to begin or start.

questions.question: Which word from the text means 'severe mental suffering'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: anguish - severe mental suffering.

questions.question: Gandhi was noted to be ______ in Arithmetic.
questions.explanation: According to accounts, he was fair in Arithmetic.

questions.question: Which nickname for Gandhi was used by his Sanskrit teacher in the role-play dialogue?
questions.explanation: The Sanskrit teacher addresses him as 'Moniya' or 'Manu'.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'merit' as mentioned in the vocabulary prefix exercise?
questions.explanation: The word 'demerit' is formed with the prefix 'de-'.

questions.question: Gandhi was the 'greatest of our independence movement' and is popularly called the ______.
questions.explanation: He is popularly called the Father of the Nation.

questions.question: At what age did Gandhi matriculate from Rajkot High School?
questions.explanation: Gandhi matriculated from this school in 1887 at the age of 18.

questions.question: What did Gandhi have 'no high regard' for during his student life?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'Though he did not have any high regard for his 'ability'...'.

questions.question: In the summary table, what is the main theme of Paragraph 5?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 of the text focuses on Gandhi's views and regrets regarding handwriting.

questions.question: What does the word 'lenient' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: lenient - not strict.

questions.question: Gandhi warns young men and women to understand that good handwriting is a ______ part of education.
questions.explanation: He warns them to 'understand that good handwriting is a necessary part of education'.

questions.question: What 'deceived' Gandhi on the Saturday he was late for gymnastics?
questions.explanation: Gandhi writes, 'I had no watch, and the cloud deceived me'.

questions.question: The Sanskrit teacher was 'grieved' because Gandhi ______.
questions.explanation: The text says, 'one day I sat in the Persian class. The Sanskrit teacher was grieved'.
B

questions.question: According to Gandhi, children should learn their letters by ______ as he does different objects.
questions.explanation: Gandhi suggests, 'Let the child learn his letters by observation'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'sacred'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: sacred - holy.

questions.question: Which event occurred first in Gandhi's life according to the text?

options.C: Seeing beautiful handwriting in South Africa

questions.explanation: Winning scholarships in the 5th standard preceded his matriculation (at 18) and his travel to England/South Africa.

questions.question: What does the word 'curriculum' mean?

options.B: A course of study in a school or college

questions.explanation: Glossary: curriculum - course of study in a school or a college.

questions.question: The Persian teacher was described as ______ to the students.
questions.explanation: The boys said the Persian teacher was 'very good and considerate to the students'.

questions.question: Gandhi writes that 'a sort of ______' was going on between the Sanskrit and Persian teachers.
questions.explanation: The text states, 'There was a sort of rivalry going on between the Sanskrit and the Persian teachers'.

questions.question: How did Gandhi feel about his teachers at high school?
questions.explanation: Gandhi writes, 'I always enjoyed the affection of my teachers'.

questions.question: Complete the phrase: 'The least little ______ drew tears from my eyes.'
questions.explanation: The text uses the word 'blemish' to describe something that upset Gandhi deeply.

questions.question: Gandhi considered himself an 'ox of a man' in what sense in his later life?

options.B: He worked like an animal in the fields.

questions.explanation: The text (quoting from A Letter to God context but applied here in exercise analysis) notes 'Lencho was an ox of a man' means working like an animal.

questions.question: Which book is NOT mentioned as one of the leading books by Mahatma Gandhi?

options.A: The Story of My Experiments with Truth

questions.explanation: 'The Golden Threshold' is by Sarojini Naidu. The others are by Gandhi.

questions.question: The headmaster Mr. Gimi was popular because he was a ______.
questions.explanation: He was popular as he was a disciplinarian, a man of method and a good teacher.

questions.question: What does the word 'retain' mean?

options.B: To continue to have or possess

questions.explanation: Glossary: retain - continue to have or possess.
